draft.title: Enrolling and voting
card: To vote in Australia, a person must be on the electoral roll. Putting your name on the roll is called enrolling.
Australian citizens must enrol once they turn 18. They can enrol from age 16, so they are ready when they turn 18.
Enrolled citizens aged 18 or over must vote in federal elections and in state and territory elections.
A person who moves house should update their enrolment, so that the roll shows where they now live.
draft.remember: Enrol at 18, or from 16 to be ready. Then vote in federal and state elections.

a.q: Priya is an Australian citizen who turns 16 next month. What can she do about the electoral roll?
opts: Enrol now, so she is ready when she turns 18
Wait, because she cannot enrol until she is 18
Enrol now and vote in the next federal election
Wait, because only people aged 21 can enrol
a.why: Citizens can enrol from age 16, so Priya is ready when she turns 18. Enrolling at 16 does not allow her to vote yet, because the duty to vote applies from 18.
a.clue: Think about the youngest age at which a citizen can enrol.

b.q: Tom is an Australian citizen who turned 18 last year. He moved from Bathurst to Newcastle and has not updated his enrolment. What should he do?
opts: Update his enrolment to show his new address
Leave it, because he only has to enrol once
Wait until he turns 21 before he updates it
Update it only if he plans to vote in a state election
b.why: Tom should update his enrolment so the roll shows where he now lives. Enrolling once is not enough if his address changes, and the same roll is used for federal and state elections.
b.clue: The roll needs to show where a person lives now.

a.best: Enrol now, so she is ready when she turns 18

b.best: Update his enrolment to show his new address
